name: frontend
//overrides: Transitive advisories cleared without leaving the dependency's current
major, so no package receives an API it was not written against.
lodash   <=4.17.23      HIGH  prototype pollution (dagre -> graphlib)
js-yaml  4.0.0-4.2.0    HIGH  quadratic-complexity DoS (eslint, dev only)
postcss  <=8.5.22       HIGH  XSS via unescaped </style>. It is BOTH a
direct devDependency and vendored by next@14 (which pinned 8.4.31),
so bumping the direct pin alone left the vulnerable copy in place.
so the override pins every consumer to the same version. It was
the `$postcss` reference form until 2026-09-01: npm 10's $ref only
resolves against `dependencies`, and postcss lives in
devDependencies, so every `npm install` (as opposed to `npm ci`)
failed with 'Unable to resolve reference'. Literal now — KEEP THE
TWO PINS IN STEP when bumping postcss (here and devDependencies).
NOT overridden, on purpose:
next / eslint-config-next / glob — the only published fix is next@16,
two majors up from the pinned 14.2.35, and 14.x has no patch. The
live advisory is a DoS in the Image Optimizer via `remotePatterns`;
this app configures no `remotePatterns` and imports `next/image`
nowhere, so the vulnerable path is not reachable. Track the upgrade
as its own piece of work — bundling a two-major framework bump into
a dependency-patch change would make both harder to review.
brace-expansion — dev-only (eslint/glob), and the fixed version is
several majors above what those packages pin.
